newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BELGIUM SACK COACH VAN MOER FOR DUTCH LOSS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIUM SACK COACH VAN MOER FOR DUTCH LOSS.

text.p: Belgium soccer coach Wilfried Van Moer has been sacked after nine months in charge and replaced by Georges Leekens, coach of surprise first division leaders Mouscron, a soccer union spokesman said on Tuesday.
"Confirmed," spokesman Guido Dewindt said when asked to comment on a report in Het Volk newspaper.
He said Van Moer was sacked because of Belgium's humiliating 3-0 home defeat by the Netherlands in a World Cup qualifier last month and because of communication problems with players and the media.
Belgium, bidding to qualify for their fifth consecutive World Cup finals, are third in European qualifying group seven, behind the Netherlands and Wales.
They won their first two matches, against Turkey and San Marino, before losing to the Dutch.
"It's Belgium-Netherlands," Dewindt said. "(The union) has thought it over, what had happened, whether tactical mistakes had been made."

"A coach depends on results and losing at home against the Netherlands, a key match, endangered our World Cup participation. Now we have to win the next two away games to stay in the running for second place in the group," he said.
Belgium visit Wales in March and Turkey in April.

Dewindt said that former Belgium defender Leekens, 48, will become full-time coach with immediate effect and quit first division fledglings Mouscron, who have a four-point first-division lead over title holders Club Brugge.
Leekens' first mission will be to groom Belgium for a friendly match against Northern Ireland in Belfast on February 11, Dewindt said.
He said that Leekens' contract would run at least until the World Cup finals, adding that qualification would "probably" have been impossible with Van Moer.
Van Moer was deputy of Paul Van Himst until April last year when Van Himst was sacked after a run of poor results and friction with players.
He was initially praised for his no-nonsense approach but soon thereafter criticised for his surly attitude towards players and reporters.
He was also slammed for dropping key players including Philippe Albert and Marc Degryse in his first matches.
"One thing leads to another. If you win and you have communication problems you can accept it. But if you lose you look at other aspects too," Dewindt said.
Leekens, like Van Moer a former Belgium international, has coached a string of Belgian first division teams including Club Brugge and Anderlecht, and Trabzonspor in Turkey.
"There's work to be done, the downward spiral certainly has to be turned into an positive spiral," Leekens told RTBF radio.
